reviews.title: Why 5 stars?
reviews.text:
I’m not sure why anyone gave it Five stars when it’s one of the worst apps I’ve ever used. It’s telling me my dog should have had certain immunizations on dates that were before he was even born in red and there’s no way to check the ones that he has had. The ones he has had just have a red exclamation point next to them as if they still needed to be done. Some of this may be the fault of the vets office but there doesn’t seem to be any way to clear it up. There’s no way for me to update his weight. There’s no way for me to make the necessary corrections. There should be a place to say he had a visit on this date with a list of what  immunizations he received. The dates they give us for our next appointment are after the dates he’s supposed to receive his next shots and so I get the red alert saying he’s past due and it stays there indefinitely. This is the worst way to keep track of my dog’s health. I’d rather go back to the handwritten record that you carry around with you than to deal with this app. I find it clumsy and frustrating and confusing because there is no way to correct any of the mistakes.
😩 this app needs a serious overhaul or the office staff at my vets place need a lesson on using the app.

reviews.title: Major flaw in giving pet medications
reviews.text: There is a major flaw in this app when giving your pets medications. First, it does not act like the Apple health app so that you can log the exact time when the medication was taken or, in this case, given to your pet. This means that if you set up the medication to give it every day at noon, but you don't give it until 3:40 PM, the medication is still going to show as though it was given at noon. For certain medications that are time sensitive, you want to make sure they are only given every 24 hours. It's very important to keep track of the exact time the medication was taken. This is a fatal flaw in this app, especially for cats on chemotherapy. In addition, there should be an Apple Watch app with a complication for pet owners to use.

reviews.title: Wow, invasive
reviews.text:
Wow, invasive
Very, very invasive. 
I read some of petvisor/Petdesk's privacy (warning) for this app. Then I ran them through Markup dot org's blacklight inspection... they are tracking everything "Blacklight detected the use of a session recorder, which tracks user mouse movement, clicks, taps, scrolls, or even network activity. This data is >>compiled into videos and heat maps that website owners can watch to see how users interact with the site.<< Research has shown these practices can be insecure and make sensitive user data such as passwords and credit card information more vulnerable to leaks."
From the apps' privacy page...
"...If you are a veterinary clinic customer accessing or using our Products, we collect specific personal data from you on behalf of your veterinary clinic. This personal data includes your first name, last name, age, birthdate, email address(es), phone number(es), residential addresses), country, geolocation data, internet protocol address, unique ID(s), mobile device ID(s), username, password, call history (Outbound, inbound, missed, and returned), call recordings, appointment history (Upcoming appointments and last appointment, previous appointments), and consent for marketing campaigns by the clinic.
Additionally, we gather information about your pet collected on behalf of the clinic through our platforms, including pet name, species, breed, sex, age, insurance, microchip number, appointments, vaccines, Rabies tag, and medical history. We might also collect your financial payment."
Call history???
Call recordings???
Yeah, no.
My dog needs HIPPA.
We have had this veterinarian for quite a while (moved here for a promo) and have been very impressed with the clinic and doctors — until I met this app which they are using. Now, I feel like there might be a trustworthyness question.

reviews.title: All Pet-Related Apps Should Have a Memorial Function

After he died, and no longer was an active pet of mine at my vet clinic that uses this platform, his entire profile was deleted without my knowledge or say-so for my account. It feels like losing him all over again. What a stupid, stupid oversight. I should be able to access his profile, the picture I uploaded for him, and any of his records, whenever I please—regardless of whether or not he is still alive and in need of care. *PETCO*, of all companies, has this function! It is absolutely inexcusable for a veterinary care app to not have the option to memorialize your pet’s profile as well. This has been so distressing I am seriously considering switching vets to a clinic that does not use PetDesk. The development team should be ashamed of themselves.

reviews.title: The EMR comes to vets
reviews.text:
The electronic medical record has done nothing but degrade the patient and physician experience in health care for humans. I hate to see it metastasizing into our otherwise wonderful vet care. Though the animals don’t care, I sent a message days ago about a medication issue and have heard nothing back. Fortunately something I was able to work out myself (I think) but the lack of response doesn’t reassure. I do not blame the vet. Human docs hate the amount of time EHR takes — my PCP shouldn’t be emailing me at 9:30 pm— and how it paradoxically distracts from the physician-pt connection and doesn’t focus of actual care, bec these programs are developed to prompt and capture chargeables. The human ones don't convince us that they consulted people doing the care. 
Yay, progress. We’ll see what happens.
